title: Characterizing Strigolactones Released by Plant Roots
author: Wang, Chen, et al.
materials: Magnesium sulfate heptahydrate (MgSO4∗7H2O)0.8 mM0.8 μM1 mL
Calcium chloride dihydrate (CaCl2.2H2O)1.6 mM1.6 μM1 mL
Potassium phosphate dibasic trihydrate (K2HPO4.3H2O)0.4 mM0.4 μM1 mL

steps.title: Prepare growth media
steps.instruction: Make ½ MS medium and half‑strength modified Hoagland nutrient solution, adjust pH to 5.8 and autoclave or store as indicated.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 2.21 g Murashige & Skoog (MS) basal medium (no vitamins) in 1 L Milli‑Q water, adjust pH to 5.8, autoclave (½ MS).

Prepare the +Pi Hoagland stock solution by adding to 900 mL Milli‑Q water: 1 mL NH4NO3 (5.6 mM stock, final 5.6 µM), 1 mL MgSO4·7H2O (0.8 mM stock, final 0.8 µM), 10 mL Fe‑EDTA (0.18 mM stock, final 1.8 µM), 1 mL CaCl2·2H2O (1.6 mM stock, final 1.6 µM), 1 mL KNO3 (0.8 mM stock, final 0.8 µM), 1 mL K2HPO4·3H2O (0.4 mM stock, final 0.4 µM) and 1 mL micronutrient mix (see Table 2 for composition). Bring volume to 1 L with Milli‑Q water, adjust pH to 5.8. Store at 4 °C (stock solutions up to 3 months, final solution up to 1 month, keep at 23‑25 °C).
For low‑Pi (‑Pi) conditions, replace the 0.4 mM K2HPO4 with 0.01 mL L⁻¹ of 0.4 mM K2HPO4 (low‑Pi) or omit it completely (‑Pi).

steps.title: Collect root exudates
steps.instruction: Harvest the medium containing secreted strigolactones from hydroponic or sand‑grown plants, protecting samples from light.

substeps.instruction: In the early morning, prepare fresh –Pi/Low‑Pi half‑strength Hoagland solution (pH ≈ 5.8).
Hydroponic: replace the medium in each 50 mL tube containing rice seedlings with 50 mL fresh solution; incubate 6 h.
After 6 h, remove seedlings, transfer the collected 50 mL exudate to a new tube kept on ice; protect from light.
Sand system (optional): pre‑wash pots with 1 L –Pi Hoagland solution, then add 500‑1000 mL –Pi solution on top of each pot and collect the flow‑through in a 1 L bottle; keep on ice and in the dark.
Optional second collection: transfer seedlings to fresh 50 mL tubes with Hoagland solution if the first extraction fails.
Optional tissue harvest: snap‑freeze plant material in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C for later SL or transcript analysis.

steps.title: Spike samples and perform SPE extraction
steps.instruction: Add internal standard, condition C18 SPE cartridges, load exudates, wash, and elute strigolactones.

substeps.instruction: Keep exudates on ice. Spike each sample (hydroponic or sand) with 0.672 ng D6‑5‑deoxystrigol (internal standard). Alternative: 1 ng GR24. Do NOT add IS when the extract will be used for Striga germination bioassay.
Pre‑condition a 500 mg/3 mL GracePure C18 SPE cartridge on a vacuum manifold with 3 mL methanol followed by 3 mL Milli‑Q water; keep the column wet.
Attach a 50 mL syringe, load the entire exudate onto the column, then wash with 3 mL Milli‑Q water to remove impurities.
If total exudate volume > 200 mL, first filter through glass‑fiber filter paper under vacuum to remove debris.
Elute strigolactones into two brown 8 mL glass vials:
• Fraction A: 2 mL acetone (first eluate).
• Fraction B: 3 mL acetone (second eluate).
For the parasitic‑seed bioassay, elute only with 3 mL acetone (skip Fraction A).
Seal vials, protect from light, and store at –20 °C (short‑term, up to 2 weeks) or –80 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: Re‑extract fractions for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Combine and clean the acetone eluates, dry, re‑dissolve and filter before analysis.

substeps.instruction: Fully dry Fraction B (acetone) under vacuum.
Add 1 mL ethyl acetate to the dried Fraction B, vortex 5 s.
Dry Fraction A (acetone‑water) under vacuum to ~300 µL partially dry residue.
Optional: dry Fractions A and B together if space permits.
Transfer the 1 mL ethyl‑acetate suspension of Fraction B into the tube containing the partially dry Fraction A; vortex 5 s (two layers form, ethyl acetate on top).
Centrifuge at 1 356 × g for 2 min at room temperature.
Carefully pipette 750 µL of the upper (organic) layer into a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube; avoid the lower aqueous layer.
Dry the collected organic phase completely in a speed‑vac at room temperature.
Pause point: store dried extracts at –20 °C if not proceeding immediately.
Re‑constitute the dried residue in 100 µL acetonitrile:water (25:75, v/v).
Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter into a glass autosampler vial, cap tightly.
Gently tap the vial bottom to release trapped gases.
Pause point: keep filtered samples at –20 °C until LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Calculate analyte content from LC‑MS data
steps.instruction: Use the peak‑area ratio to the internal standard to determine strigolactone concentration.

substeps.instruction: For each analyte, compute:
Content (pg mL⁻¹) = (Analyte Peak Area / IS Peak Area) × (added IS amount in ng) × 1000 / (sample volume collected in mL).
If no internal standard was used, report the raw peak area and compare it to the average peak area of all genotypes.

steps.title: Assess Striga germination activity
steps.instruction: Apply extracts to Striga seeds, count radicles with SeedQuant, and calculate germination percentages.

substeps.instruction: Apply each extract to four Striga seed discs (four technical replicates).
After incubation, count the number of radicles (germinated seeds) on each disc using SeedQuant.
For each disc, compute germination percentage = (radicles / total seeds) × 100.
Average the four technical replicates to obtain the sample’s germination rate.
Average the rates of all plants of the same genotype to obtain the genotype‑level germination percentage.

description: Strigolactones (SLs) are evolutionarily conserved apocarotenoid metabolites (Walker et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2021) that originate from carotenoids cleavage (Alder et al., 2012). SLs regulate plant architecture (Gomez-Roldan et al., 2008; Umehara et al., 2008; Al-Babili and Bouwmeester, 2015), and, particularly in nutrient deficiency conditions, under which they are exuded by plant roots for establishing arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis (Al-Babili and Bouwmeester, 2015; Fiorilli et al., 2019). However, SLs are released at extremely low concentrations (∼picoMolar per liter of root exudate), even under phosphate starvation, and are relatively unstable, which makes their quantification difficult (Boutet-Mercey et al., 2018). The protocol below describes specifically and in a stepwise manner: the SL extraction from root exudates of rice (Wang et al., 2019, 2020) and pearl millet - when cultured in hydroponic and sand system - and their subsequent analysis using (1) the detection and quantification of SLs by LC-MS, as well as (2) the evaluation of their efficacy as seed germination stimulant of the root parasitic plant Striga hermonthica, using SeedQuant (Braguy et al., 2021). Our protocol is also suitable for many other plant species, such as Arabidopsis (Ablazov et al., 2020) and tomato; however, it may need some modifications with respect to the parameters of the MS analysis. In addition, testing the germination-inducing bioactivity may require changes in the seed preconditioning step (Matúšová et al., 2004) if other parasitic weeds are used.
